subject: MAP sprint stall — request to rebaseline close and runbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@helixtx.com>, procurement@helixtx.com
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP sprint stall — request to rebaseline close and runbook

Hi Susan / Helix procurement team,

Quick note from the MAP weekly — we hit a hard stall on the procurement sign-off that blocks our acceptance window. Procurement indicated a departmental budget review has pushed their PO approval into the week of June 23, which cascades our current cutover slot out by ~3 weeks.

We want to be proactive: attached is an updated MAP ("MAP_v2.xlsx") and a short risk catalog with mitigation options. Can you confirm the procurement ETA and whether a conditioned PO (covering initial API license + reserved capacity) is possible to keep current cutovers? If not, we need to discuss a rebaseline for the close date and a short-term contingency (partial acceptance / canary cutover) to preserve momentum.

To surface options:
- Confirmed procurement ETA (date) and any blockers
- If sign-off delayed >14 days, Helix: would you consider executing a limited-scope PO covering the pilot tranche?
- Redwood: we'll propose a rebaseline with phased acceptance windows and a credit runway if the go-live shifts beyond 30 days.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with phased windows) and Risk_Catalog.pdf (initial assessment).

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our engineering hold and resource scheduling.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (Excel, 78KB)]
[Attachment: Risk_Catalog.pdf (PDF, 124KB)]

From: Susan Park <susan.park@helixtx.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixtx.com
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sprint stall — request to rebaseline close and runbook

Naomi — thanks for the heads up and for sending the MAP. Short summary from our side:

- We are in a final departmental budget alignment meeting; finance asked to defer any non-critical committals until after the June 20 exec review.
- Procurement can produce a conditioned PO but requires legal to sign next week; that process is likely to take 7–10 business days.

Given that, my current read is the earliest firm PO we can expect is the week of June 23. I know that pushes your window. Two asks from Helix: 1) can Redwood hold the current go-live slot for a short period while we finalize legal? 2) If not, please propose the phased acceptance plan so we can evaluate smaller-scope PO options.

I reviewed the MAP_v2 spreadsheet and the phased windows look reasonable — thank you. I attached the internal procurement timing doc for context.

I appreciate the flexibility; will update you by end-of-day Monday with any movement.

Best,
Susan Park
Director, IT Procurement — Helix Therapeutics
[Attachment: PO_timing.pdf (PDF, 46KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@helixtx.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP sprint stall — request to rebaseline close and runbook

On Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 09:32 Susan Park <susan.park@helixtx.com> wrote:
> Naomi — thanks for the heads up and for sending the MAP. Short summary from our side:
> - We are in a final departmental budget alignment meeting; finance asked to defer any non-critical committals until after the June 20 exec review.
> - Procurement can produce a conditioned PO but requires legal to sign next week; that process is likely to take 7–10 business days.
>
> Given that, my current read is the earliest firm PO we can expect is the week of June 23.

Susan — appreciate the transparency. I've attached a concise risk catalog and three rebaseline scenarios for your team to review (Rebaseline_Scenarios.docx). High-level recommendation from Redwood engineering and CS: we introduce a phased acceptance approach to preserve the June engineering hold while avoiding a full capacity reservation. Suggested options: 

Scenario A — Hold current June cutover (best effort): Redwood reserves engineering time for a one-week canary; Helix provides a conditioned PO covering pilot license (30% of committed capacity). If PO doesn't convert to full PO within 30 days, Redwood offers a one-time service credit to Helix.

Scenario B — Rebaseline close to July 21: Move formal close + final acceptance to July 21 with staggered acceptance windows (pilot -> scale). Redwood will keep the configuration snapshot; a small hold fee applies.

Scenario C — Split-go-live (targeted features first): Ship the critical inference endpoints first (read-only), follow with write-path and analytics in second tranche — reduces immediate procurement size.

We recommend Scenario B as the pragmatic default unless Helix can commit the conditioned PO this week. For clarity, the proposed rebaseline table and credit runway are in Rebaseline_Scenarios.docx and Risk_Catalog.pdf.

Attachments: Rebaseline_Scenarios.docx, Risk_Catalog.pdf.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Rebaseline_Scenarios.docx (DOCX, 96KB)]
[Attachment: Risk_Catalog.pdf (PDF, 124KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Helix MAP stall — request for exec approval on contingency credit and hold

Team — looping you in. Helix procurement has deferred non-critical commitments until after their June 20 exec review; earliest PO we're seeing is week of June 23. We have proposed three scenarios (A/B/C) — Rishi prefers Scenario B (rebaseline to July 21) unless Helix can supply a conditioned PO this week.

Action items I need from leadership:
- Approve a one-time service credit up to 10% if Helix's go-live slips beyond 30 days (to be offered as a sales concession and logged against HLX-4532).
- Approve a temporary engineering hold (2 FTE equivalents for one sprint) to keep the June canary slot reserved while we confirm procurement. This should be chargeable to the deal hold budget.
- If credit/hold approved, authorize Camila to sign the conditional hold agreement with procurement when they provide an initial PO.

Why escalate now: if we don't protect the canary window within 48 hours the engineering calendar will be reallocated and the effective slip will grow beyond the 3-week estimate. Helix is a mid-market strategic account — preserving momentum is high value.

Naomi (copied: Rishi for technical details)
Naomi Feldman | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Internal note: proposed credit tracked in sales concessions; Camila to document conditional hold agreement]
